question_text: According to the course material, Nigeria's manufacturing industries are broadly divided into light industries and:
option_a: Heavy industries, such as iron and steel, chemical manufacturing, and shipbuilding
explanation: Manufacturing is divided into light industries (textiles, printing, furniture, food processing, electronics) and heavy industries (iron and steel, chemical manufacturing, copper and aluminium smelting, shipbuilding).

question_text: According to the course material, early modern manufacturing developments in Nigeria in the 1920s included the introduction of the hand oil press for palm oil extraction and:
option_a: Modern ginneries for extracting cotton lint from seed cotton
option_b: The country's first automobile assembly plant
option_c: The country's first crude oil refinery
explanation: By the 1920s, the hand oil press was introduced for better palm oil extraction, and modern ginneries were introduced for extracting cotton lint from seed cotton, both early developments in modern manufacturing.

question_text: According to the course material, after the Second World War and especially in the 1950s, Nigeria formally adopted which industrialisation strategy?
option_a: Import substitution, aiming to produce locally as many imported consumer goods as possible
option_b: Complete reliance on imported manufactured goods with no local production
option_c: Exclusive focus on exporting only raw, unprocessed materials
option_d: Total nationalisation of all existing colonial-era businesses
explanation: After World War II, especially in the 1950s, Nigeria adopted the import substitution strategy of industrialisation, aiming to produce locally as many as possible of the consumer goods that were being imported.

question_text: According to the course material, by 1970, how many industrial plants did Nigeria have?
explanation: By 1970, Nigeria had more than 700 industrial plants, reflecting the growth of manufacturing establishments since the country adopted the import substitution strategy in the 1950s.

question_text: According to the course material, traditional industries in Nigeria, distinct from modern manufacturing, date back to prehistoric times and include leather works, textile works, and:
option_a: Brass, gold, silver, and bronze works
explanation: Traditional industries dating back to prehistoric times include the processing of agricultural food products, leather works, textile works, and brass, gold, silver, and bronze works, among other cottage crafts.
